name: fee_quote_25bps
description: Pure integer fee quote transition for a fixed 25 basis point fee rate. The input state is the previous quote, carrying the last rounded fee units and the exact remainder of the last scaled division. The parameter is the quoted amount in unsigned 64-bit units. The scaled amount is amount * 25 (basis points scale) and the divisor is 10000: units = scaled / 10000 truncating toward zero, remainder = scaled % 10000, which is retained exactly so that units * 10000 + remainder = scaled. A zero amount is a valid quote yielding zero units and zero remainder. If the scaled amount would exceed the unsigned 64-bit range (amount * 25 > 18446744073709551615), every field of the prior quote is preserved unchanged. This is a pure calculation only: account authorization, persistence and settlement are outside this project's scope.
specification: if amount * 25 <= 18446744073709551615 then { units := (amount * 25) / 10000, remainder := (amount * 25) % 10000 } else { units := s.units, remainder := s.remainder }

properties.name: overflow_preserves_quote
properties.description: When the scaled amount would overflow the unsigned 64-bit range, every field of the prior quote is carried over unchanged.

properties.name: reconstructs_scaled_amount
properties.description: For a successful quote, the rounded units and the retained remainder reconstruct the scaled amount exactly: units * 10000 + remainder = amount * 25.

properties.name: remainder_below_divisor
properties.description: For a successful quote the retained remainder is strictly less than the divisor 10000.

properties.name: prior_quote_wellformed
properties.description: A well formed prior quote (remainder below the divisor) stays well formed after the transition, including on the overflow path where the prior quote is preserved.

properties.name: zero_amount_valid_quote
properties.description: A zero amount is a valid quote: it produces zero units and zero remainder rather than an error or an overflow fallback.

assumptions: The fee rate is fixed at 25 basis points: the scaled amount is amount * 25 and the divisor is 10000, so units = scaled / 10000 and remainder = scaled % 10000 with truncation toward zero.
All amounts, units and remainders are unsigned 64-bit integers; the mathematical specification reasons over exact natural numbers and never wraps.

The overflow guard amount * 25 <= 18446744073709551615 is equivalent to amount <= 737869762948382064, the exact floor of the unsigned 64-bit maximum divided by 25, so the implementation performs no wrapping multiplication.
The state is the previous quote: a genuine prior quote satisfies s.remainder < 10000. The transition preserves such a prior quote unchanged on overflow.
Scope is the pure calculation only. Account authorization, persistence, settlement, rounding policies other than truncation toward zero, and any variable fee rate are outside this project's scope.
